details:
The SDK's default Additive controller has a single layer with blending mode **Additive**, and both of its states ("Upright Idle", "Empty") are **Write Defaults OFF**.

When no WD OFF state in a playable layer above Additive covers it, every shape key that is bound by some clip in the avatar's playable layers and has a non-zero value on the SkinnedMeshRenderer is shown at **3×** its value (30 → 90).

We observed this in the VRChat client on an affected avatar, and reproduced it with the minimal steps below in Gesture Manager.

Setting only the Additive controller's states to Write Defaults ON fixes it without changing the idle body motion.

### Steps to reproduce

Unity 2022.3.22f1, VRChat SDK Avatars 3.10.4, Gesture Manager 3.9.9

1. Use any humanoid avatar. On its face SkinnedMeshRenderer, set any shape key to **30**.

2. Create an FX controller with one layer (weight 1):

   - a default state "Idle" with an empty clip, **WD ON**;

   - a state "Shape" whose clip animates that shape key, **WD ON**, with no transitions into it (it never plays).

   Assign it to the FX slot.

3. Duplicate `Packages/com.vrchat.avatars/Samples/AV3 Demo Assets/Animation/Controllers/vrc_AvatarV3HandsLayer.controller`, enable **Write Defaults on every state**, and assign it to the Gesture slot (mask `vrc_HandsOnly`).

4. Leave Base, Additive, Action, Sitting, TPose and IKPose at their defaults.

5. Play and stand idle with no gesture.

   - **Expected:** 30

   - **Actual:** **90**

6. Duplicate `vrc_AvatarV3IdleLayer.controller`, enable Write Defaults on both states, and assign it to the Additive slot.

   - **Actual:** 30. The idle body motion is unchanged.

Notes:

- Only shape keys bound by some clip in the playable layers are affected, even if that clip never plays. A value of 0 stays 0.

- Base does not matter.

- It is masked while any WD OFF state plays above Additive (default Gesture, a WD OFF FX, or Action at weight 1 during an emote/AFK). This is why most avatars never notice.

### Why

A WD OFF state asserts every animated binding of the avatar and fills the ones it does not animate with its held (bind-time) value.

On the additive Additive input, that dense pose is added on top of the lower layers — once through the additive input, once more through the additive layer blend.

A shape key the Additive layer never touches therefore still receives its default value twice: **d + 2d = 3d**.

With an empty (zero-curve) clip in the same state, the value diverges instead of settling.

### Why WD ON is safe for this controller

We compared Additive = default (WD OFF) against a WD ON copy across every combination of:

- Base {WD OFF, ON}

- Gesture {WD OFF, ON}

- FX {WD OFF, ON, mixed per layer}

- Action weight {0, 1}

That is 24 configurations, 300 frames each, over all 54 humanoid bones and the root, using a muscle-only additive idle clip that moves the body by up to 8°.

| | Additive WD OFF (default) | Additive WD ON |

| --- | --- | --- |

| Shape keys | 3× in the configurations with WD ON Gesture and FX and Action at weight 0; 1× elsewhere | **1× in all 24** |

| Humanoid motion | reference | **identical in all 24** (0° / 0 m difference) |

Humanoid muscles are a single human pose that is not affected by Write Defaults, so the idle motion does not depend on this setting.

On WD OFF avatars the change is invisible; on WD ON avatars it removes the error.

Tools already apply this fix: VRCFury's "Fix Write Defaults" marks all additive states WD ON.

### Request

Set Write Defaults ON on both states of the SDK's default Additive controller (and the client's internal equivalent, if it mirrors the SDK asset).

### Related

"[BUG] VRChat apply blend shape values 3 times" (2020, marked fixed) — same symptom; the cause described here is in the default controller asset.

https://feedback.vrchat.com/avatar-30/p/bug-vrchat-apply-blend-shape-values-3-times
title: SDK default Additive controller (vrc_AvatarV3IdleLayer) uses Write Defaults OFF on an additive layer, tripling non-zero blendshapes
